The Mother of God: Unexpected Joy

Icons

Theotokos

The Mother of God: Unexpected Joy

Nechayannaya Radost

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Judges 6:36–40

King James Version · Scripture previews

The OCA connects Unexpected Joy with a story recorded by Saint Demetrius of Rostov in The Fleece of Prayer. The joy in this narrative is the forgiveness received by a repentant sinner. Its printed principal commemoration is December 9.

[1] Heading; opening and second paragraphs

What is depicted

The composition contains an icon within the icon: a youth kneels in a room before an image of the Mother of God and Christ. Wounds appear on the Child’s hands, feet, and side as the narrative unfolds.

[1] Opening paragraph and youth narrative

History and tradition

In the published account, the young man has a devotion to the Theotokos while continuing to plan sinful acts. One day, before going out to sin, he sees blood flowing from Christ’s wounds. He asks who has caused them and hears that he and other sinners crucify her Son again. The encounter brings recognition of his conduct and prolonged, tearful repentance. The story ends with mercy and forgiveness, rather than merely with his surprise at a miraculous sight.

[1] Second paragraph, from the youth’s prayer to forgiveness

Published explanation

The OCA also prints January 25 and May 1 as commemorations. Its reference to Judges 6:36–40 identifies the scriptural fleece associated with the book’s title; that passage is not the biblical narration of this later icon story.

[1] Opening paragraph’s bracketed reference; final paragraph
